target.fixture: disposable loopback container with temporary storage

passed_cases.evidence: Principal-owned application state and the LangGraph checkpoint schema survived adapter reconstruction
Sessions, Portfolios, Snapshots, Goal contexts, Runs, RunEvents, History, Inspector traces, SSE replay, and idempotency remained durable and cross-Principal requests returned not-found responses
a running Run older than the request deadline became an immutable safe failed result with RUN_INTERRUPTED; a fresh running Run remained untouched
one observed expiry time removed the Session cascade and checkpoint thread; a second execution made no further changes
the verify-only runtime role served identity, Session, and Run requests with DML grants while PostgreSQL rejected CREATE TABLE

the owner policy granted only database/schema access, the migration identity installed default privileges for its own objects, runtime could use DML but not DDL, and retention could select/delete but not insert or create

two isolated Principals, Portfolios, Snapshots, Goal contexts, Runs, RunEvents, and checkpoint threads survived adapter restart; an independent recovery phase found all markers and the retention phase removed the expired thread before final synthetic cleanup
the authenticated readiness response reported the PostgreSQL application and checkpoint schemas compatible

limits: The fixture is not Cloud SQL staging.
The fixture does not qualify automated backup, point-in-time recovery, RPO, RTO, rollout capacity, or regional recovery.
The application and checkpoint saver still use separate transactions; whole-Run atomicity is not claimed.
Qdrant authenticated readiness and collection recovery are outside this artifact.
